target_definition.crowd_score_normalized: SYNTHETIC. Formula: (annual_visitors/365 * season_mult * weekend_mult * holiday_mult * noise) / capacity_per_day, clipped to [0,1]. See simulate_crowd_data.py. Not an observed real-world value.
target_definition.risk_level: Threshold of crowd_score_normalized (>=0.75 High, >=0.45 Medium, else Low).

target_leakage_note: is_weekend, is_public_holiday, season and capacity_per_day are direct ingredients of the generating formula and are also model features; hotel_occupancy_rate and daily_flights_at_cmb are generated from the same drivers. Measured with scripts/validate_model.py (2026-10-01): dropping capacity_per_day lowered site-holdout R2 from 0.3331 to -0.3630 and site-grouped CV (repeat 0, 5 folds) R2 from 0.555 to 0.295, so skill on unseen destinations depends mainly on this formula ingredient. Dropping occupancy+flights, is_weekend+is_public_holiday, or season individually changed R2 by about 0.01 or less, but month and day_of_week still carry equivalent information, so those tests cannot show the features are harmless. Random-split and date-block metrics are optimistic; report site-holdout and site-grouped CV.
encoding_note: OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore') is used for category/season/district instead of LabelEncoder, to avoid an arbitrary integer ordering of nominal categories and to encode an unseen category as an all-zero row instead of silently mapping it to 0. Earlier notes quoted site-holdout R2 values of 0.68-0.91 and about 0.87-0.89; those came from an earlier experiment configuration and are NOT reproduced by this pipeline. The verified site-holdout R2 with this encoding is 0.3331.
hyperparameter_selection_note: n_estimators=50, max_depth=12, min_samples_split=7 were chosen by a 3-fold random-row GridSearchCV on a random 80% split that included the 10 holdout sites (values lie on the grid edge). scripts/validate_model.py Section 6 repeated the search with site-grouped folds and no holdout sites: it selected near-identical settings (inner MAE 0.1153 vs 0.1155; holdout R2 0.3351 vs 0.3331), so the parameters are locked.
deployment_model_note: models/crowd_pipeline.pkl and risk_pipeline.pkl are trained on a random 80% of rows from all 197 sites, including the 10 holdout sites. The site-holdout metrics come from a separate model trained without those sites, which is not saved.

site_holdout_evaluation.description: Entire sites held out of training. Tests generalization to unseen destinations (10 fixed sites: 4 Beach, 4 Nature, 1 Heritage, 1 Religious; harder than average).

site_grouped_cv_evaluation.description: Site-grouped CV over all 197 sites, 5 folds x 3 repeats; every site is unseen once per repeat. Folds overlap across repeats, so the sd is a spread, not a confidence interval.

date_block_cv_evaluation.description: 5-fold CV without shuffling, in file order. The data file is sorted by date, so each fold is a contiguous block of dates and every site appears in training. Optimistic; not a test of unseen destinations.

random_split_evaluation.description: Random 80/20 row split. The same sites appear in train and test, so this is optimistic (site-level memorisation plus formula ingredients). Do not report as the primary metric.

independent_validation.note: Temporal 2024->2025, baselines, ablation, shuffled-target check, error analysis and calibration are computed there, not here.

limitations: crowd_score_normalized is synthetic; no metric measures agreement with real crowds.
Skill on unseen destinations depends heavily on capacity_per_day, an ingredient of the target's generating formula.
Errors on unseen destinations are mostly site-level offsets; annual visitors is not a model input.
Temporal 2024->2025 validation is nearly identical to a random split because the simulator reuses one formula in both years.
The deployed model was trained on rows from all 197 sites, including the 10 holdout sites.
